When I first watched this movie, I had two takeaways: Joaquin Phoneix stole the show, and the emotional impact of the ending made up for an otherwise forgettable story. This time around, I'm realizing the story isn't really forgettable, just non-existent. Maximus's journey has no significant beats in between his betrayal and victory; he just...does well. He's presented fairly flawless in a story that renders him pretty passive. There's some exchanges that would have us believe that loses his honor in slavery, but I don't think it's a stretch to say he acts out of reason (besides kissing his ex, which the movie presents as romantic and not a betrayal of the dead wife he keeps talking about). I still think Phoenix has the more interesting character. As for the ending, yes it is beautiful, but I'm starting to realize how much it's carried by Zimmer.

Extrem plotfokussierter Historien-Action-Schinken, der harte Spuren des Kinos der späten 90er enthält. Insbesondere visuell wird das mit zahlreichen Zeitlupen und Inserts sichtbar, die Tiefe und eine Traumebene zeigen sollen. Auditiv natürlich auch, denn Hans Zimmer dudelt uns fast ununterbrochen seine Spätromantik in die Ohren, damit wir auch ja nicht verpassen, wie wir uns gerade zu fühlen haben. Interessant auch, wie viele der Motive und Versatzstücke späterer Erfolge (insbesondere Fluch der Karibik) schon hier vorkommen. Dramaturgisch fand ich den Film gelinde gesagt schwach, weil er sich überhaupt keine Zeit nimmt, um irgendwo Tiefe bei Situationen oder Charakteren aufkommen zu lassen (mit Ausnahme des Helden Maximus und des Antagonisten Commodus). Sämtliche Nebencharaktere werden so zur Dekoration, die als Staffage in den einzelnen Nummern auftauchen, in denen Schlacht an Kampf an Training an Kampf aneinandergereiht werden. Muss ehrlicherweise auch zugeben, dass ich zwischenzeitlich eingenickt bin, was auch nicht für den Film spricht. Aber so bleibt ein leider weitestgehend ahistorischer Schinken, dem noch die dramaturgische Reife späterer Versuche in dem Genre fehlt und dessen Stärken wie üblich eigentlich nur in technischen Kategorien liegt.

ANÁLISE DO FILME "GLADIADOR" O filme Gladiador, dirigido por Ridley Scott e lançado em 2000, retrata a Roma Antiga durante o período do Império Romano, acompanhando a trajetória de Maximus, um general romano que é traído pelo imperador Cômodo e acaba escravizado e transformado em gladiador. A obra permite identificar diferentes aspectos da sociedade romana e como sua política funcionava na prática. A narrativa inicia-se com a batalha das tropas romanas contra os povos germânicos. Após a vitória de Roma, o imperador Marco Aurélio convida Maximus a ser seu sucessor para combater a corrupção do Senado, alegando que Cômodo era incapaz de governar; entretanto, Maximus recusa a proposta. Movido pela ganância, Cômodo decide assassinar o próprio pai para reivindicar o trono, além de exilar Maximus e ordenar a execução de sua esposa e de seu filho. Maximus consegue fugir, mas, gravemente ferido, acaba desmaiando no deserto. Encontrado por comerciantes de escravos, ele é levado até Zucabar, onde é vendido a Próximo, um proprietário de gladiadores. Agora conhecido como "Hispânico", Maximus participa relutantemente de pequenas batalhas, atraindo os olhares da multidão por sua força e habilidades surpreendentes. Percebendo o potencial do lutador, Próximo o leva para o Coliseu, palco dos grandes eventos coordenados por Cômodo. Maximus vence a batalha final e se revela ao imperador, que fica indignado ao saber que ele continua vivo. Ao descobrir que seu antigo general estava bem, Cícero se encontra com Maximus para traçar um plano de fuga e libertá-lo da escravidão. Ao descobrir a conspiração, Cômodo manda matar Cícero e seus companheiros. Decidido a recuperar sua honra diante dos súditos, o imperador resolve enfrentar Maximus pessoalmente, ferindo-o traiçoeiramente na noite anterior ao combate para obter vantagem. Apesar dos ferimentos, Maximus consegue derrotar Cômodo utilizando a própria adaga do imperador. Em seus últimos momentos de vida, pede que seus companheiros sejam libertados e que Roma volte a ser governada sem corrupção. O filme se encerra mostrando Maximus no pós-vida finalmente se reencontrando com sua esposa e filho. Com essa breve análise do filme, podemos traçar paralelos entre o conteúdo do filme e a história real. Logo nas primeiras cenas, somos apresentados a uma característica marcante do Império Romano: suas guerras incessantes em busca de expansão territorial. Outro ponto crucial é o pedido de Marcus Aurélio a Maximus para que ele assuma o trono e erradique a corrupção do Senado, restaurando Roma à sua forma republicana original. Isso contrasta com a visão de Cômodo, que desejava que Roma permanecesse um império. À medida que a história se desenrola, testemunhamos o funcionamento do comércio escravista quando Maximus é capturado e vendido como gladiador. Isso destaca ainda mais outro aspecto do Império: a política do Pão e Circo, que desempenhou um papel significativo na ascensão de Maximus como gladiador. A crescente popularidade de Maximus alarmou Cômodo, levando-o a tomar decisões desesperadas que resultaram em sua morte. Review pra trabalho de historia

Evidentemente es una gran película, empecemos por ahí, pues la historia ya se ha encargado de ponerla en ese puesto. Sin embargo tengo algunas discrepancias con algunas decisiones creativas del film. Principalmente me ha parecido normal que sea la película favorita de padres por excelencia, pues me parece una película que apunta a un público algo acostumbrado a holliwoodeces donde la información se da tan mascada que roza lo propagandístico, donde te dejan claro quien es el malo y quien es el héroe, ya que el protagonista es el arquetipo clásico de héroe honorable hasta el punto de lo inverosímil. Es decir, retrata lo que “debe ser un hombre”. Siempre me llama la atención como esta figura trata de ser representada de maneras tan contradictorias tratando de retratar de manera piadosa y gentil a una figura que, bajo justificaciones del guión, se las pasa matando a gente de una manera ciertamente enajenada, pues todo cuanto hace es por servidumbre a los de arriba (ya digo, de manera propagandística en base a los valores tradicionales) en la primera parte de la película. Creo que su mayor pecado es glorificar este tipo de arquetipo heróico casi infantilizado al dar mascado a tal exceso que no cabe interpretación más que la dada de quien es el objetivamente bueno y el objetivamente malo. Creo que también la manera en la que se glorifica el antiguo imperio romano es peligrosa, pues no olvidemos que fue un imperio sujeto económicamente por la esclavitud, con gente de bajos recursos obligada a luchar hasta la muerte, sistemas de gobierno corruptos, etc. y aunque esto también sea ciertamente expresado, la realidad es que implícitamente se vanagloria. Digo esto dando por hecho que en sí, es una obra maestra y no se lo quita nadie. La banda sonora es increíblemente y tiene una fotografía espectacular. La estructura narrativa me gusta, aunque no invente nada nuevo, se ciñe bien a lo que se debe y, si eres avispado, puedes ir viendo pistas a lo largo de la peli, y empezando por la primera escena, de como será el desenlace.

Outstanding film, 5 stars for me.  I gave Gladiator 5 stars because it’s one of those films that just feels epic from start to finish. The scale of everything is amazing, from the huge battles at the beginning to the Colosseum scenes later on. Ridley Scott does a great job making Ancient Rome feel massive and dangerous, and the production design, costumes and cinematography all add to that. Even though it’s over two and a half hours long, I was completely invested in what was happening. Russell Crowe is easily one of the best things about the film. Maximus is such a likeable character because he isn’t just a stereotypical action hero; he’s driven by his family, his loyalty and his desire for revenge. Crowe gives him a quiet but powerful presence, by far his best performance I have seen. Joaquin Phoenix is also brilliant as Commodus. He’s horrible, selfish and unpredictable, but that’s exactly what makes him such an effective villain. The two performances make the rivalry between them feel personal rather than just being good guy vs bad guy. They are both absolute standout performances. The action is another massive positive for me. The opening battle is absolutely insane, and the gladiator fights are brutal but really entertaining. The way the film builds up the arena battles makes them feel like events rather than just random action scenes. Hans Zimmer’s soundtrack also deserves a lot of credit because it makes the emotional and dramatic moments hit so much harder. The film manages to combine action, drama and emotion really well, which is probably why it still has such a strong reputation with audiences today. In terms of negatives, at times, the film does feel a little slow, especially during some of the political scenes outside the arena. Some of the dialogue can also feel a bit overdramatic or predictable. However, I’d say that’s me being very picky to be honest, considering the dialogue is to fit in for the ancient Roman time period it’s set in. Overall, though, those problems don’t really stop me from giving Gladiator 5 stars. For me, it’s the combination of the performances, action, music, visuals and emotional story that makes it work so well. The ending especially gives the whole story a lot more emotional weight, and I think Gladiator is one of those films that deserves its reputation as a classic. It’s Ridley Scott at his best and the story works so well, pure entertainment and unreal storytelling, one of those movies that makes you want to be there in the moment. Easily 5 stars for me.

The AP Top 25 #4 Every time I watch, I beg Marcus Aurelius to not tell Commodus he will not be Emperor alone in the middle of the night. And yet he does, every time, without fail. But if he didn’t, I wouldn’t get to experience one of the greatest stories ever told. Maximus is probably my favorite character ever. I’ve always been fascinated by the reluctant hero archetype. One who does not wish for power, and yet it is that trait that makes them most suited for it. Maximus is the epitome of this archetype. A man who just wants to get home to his family, and yet he recognizes what he must do. "I've seen much of the rest of the world. It is brutal and cruel and dark. Rome is the light." He serves for the good of the realm, not for any personal ambition. “Strength and Honor.” A motto made up by Russell Crowe on a whim, and yet it’s perfectly summarizes the character. And on the other side of the coin, we have Commodus. A mixture of cruelty, naivety and cowardice. He is the complete opposite of Maximus. A yin to his yang. Where Maximus is quiet and contemplative, Commodus is loud and ornery. Maximus commands respect, while Commodus instills fear. Perfect personifications of the forces of good and evil. Two of my favorite acting performances ever in the same movie. This is just such a fun movie to watch. Deeply emotional and incredibly satisfying. At its most basic level, it’s a simple revenge story. But all the little details elevate it to the highest level. I love a swords and sandals epic, and there are few scales grander than the Roman Colosseum. This is one I will never get tired of watching, despite the 2.5 hour runtime.
